named.summary: One real repeat this week: Claude wrote developer docs in a hand-holding, over-explained register despite an active voice check that fires but does not always block. The two session-correction clusters carry no named mistake type and resolve to noise under the standing amendment.
named.process_note: The zero-fire diagnostic requested across the 2026w44–2026w46 amendments is still absent. This week the doc-voice-gate shows 19 blocks and 124 nudges alongside a repeat atone for the same pattern. Without a column showing exit-1 vs exit-0 vs muted counts broken down by file type, the reader cannot determine whether the gate's advisory fires on README-style files are a deliberate policy or a logic gap. That single column would have resolved the guard verdict for c-2d8458a5 from 'partly' to a precise diagnosis before the run.

proposal.change: Raise the exit code to blocking for any doc file matched by README, AGENTS, or docs/ whose tone scores as informal-explainer, rather than emitting an advisory nudge.

happened.what: Claude wrote README, AGENTS, and planning docs for a developer project in a wordy, informal, hand-holding register instead of direct developer prose.
A proposal was raised the same day to ban the coddling-explainer register from developer and agent documentation entirely.

items.why_repeats: The check's scope covers only .md files under docs/ and files that carry a non-agent reader: frontmatter tag; a root-level README, AGENTS file, or planning doc without that tag is outside the check entirely. Even for files it does reach, the fault detectors target ledger-voice markers and wall-of-text, not an informal or hand-holding prose register — so the specific failure that recurred is invisible to it on two independent grounds.
items.fix: Extend the check's scope to cover README and AGENTS files at the project root (without requiring reader: frontmatter), and add a detection path for informal-explainer register — verbose hedging, coddling phrases, over-explained steps — as a blocking fault alongside the existing ledger-voice and wall-of-text paths.

guard.plain: A check on the register and tone of documentation Claude writes
guard.gap: Root-level README and AGENTS files are outside the check's scope (it requires docs/ placement or a reader: frontmatter tag), and the check's three fault detectors — dense-block, spliced-line, mechanism-run — do not include informal or hand-holding register, so the pattern that recurred produces no signal from this check at all.
